facts.text: The borough’s name comes from Fidelus Oliphant’s promise of a “fair chance” to repay a Uniontown bank loan, a story that locals still share.
Permanent settlement began in 1752 when Wendall Brown and his sons established a homestead in Provance’s Bottom before moving to richer soils in Georges.
Early economy hinged on iron production, with Oliphant’s furnaces drawing local siderite and Mercer ores before switching to coke fuel in the 1880s.
A railroad line opened between 1877 and 1882, linking Fairchance to the Southwest Pennsylvania Railway and eventually the Baltimore & Ohio network.
Fairchance sits at the western base of Chestnut Ridge, the westernmost major ridge of the Appalachian Mountains in this part of Pennsylvania.
The historic Fairchance Furnace, once a key ironworks, shifted from using local siderite to coke fuel by the 1880s, reflecting industrial change.
